name: Indigo Gabbro
physical: Traditionally linked to a steady, grounded feeling
Associated with comfort during stressful periods
Kept nearby by many for balance and calm
summary: Indigo gabbro is a dark igneous rock flecked with white and silver, used in crystal practice for grounding, shadow work and quiet intuition.
intro: Indigo gabbro is a deep charcoal-black rock with a scatter of white to pale grey flecks, sometimes with blue or indigo tones that appear when the stone is polished. It is a coarse-grained igneous rock made largely of plagioclase feldspar and pyroxene, formed slowly from magma deep within the earth, and it is the plutonic cousin of basalt. In the crystal trade it is sold under names like mystic merlinite or indigo gabbro, and polished spheres, palm stones and tumbled pieces show off a dramatic, starry pattern. It is heavy, cool and calming to hold, and it makes an ideal low-key altar stone.
history: Gabbro takes its name from a town in Tuscany, Italy, and the term was used by Italian miners and stoneworkers to describe a dark, crystalline rock. It forms much of the oceanic crust and has been used for countertops, monuments and paving. In crystal circles, the indigo variety is marketed under several names, including indigo gabbro and mystic merlinite, and the stone is often described alongside stones with Arthurian associations because of the name merlinite, though the connection is modern rather than historical. Madagascar is a leading source of the polished pieces sold today. There is no ancient folklore, but the stone's resemblance to a night sky inspires many modern uses.
meaning: Crystal practitioners view indigo gabbro as a stone of balance between light and shadow. The black and white contrasts make it a symbol for accepting both sides of the self, which is why it is used in shadow work and personal reflection. It is considered grounding, anchoring wandering thoughts in the body, while its starry look is tied to intuition and mystery. People turn to it when they feel overwhelmed by too much input or emotional noise. It is often placed in meditation space as a quiet protector. Traditionally it is associated with steadiness, calm and a settled mood, and is kept nearby by those who want to feel centered during uncertain times.
howToUse: Hold an indigo gabbro palm stone during evening meditation and focus on the contrast of dark and light in the pattern. Place a sphere on a shelf or altar as a steady anchor, or set a tumbled stone near the front door to mark a threshold. For shadow work, sit with the stone and a notebook, writing down thoughts you usually avoid. It works well in a grid with black tourmaline and clear quartz, and it can be tucked in a bag for travel days when you want a calm, grounded companion.
care: Indigo gabbro is a hard, stable rock that tolerates a lukewarm rinse and a gentle scrub. Dry it thoroughly afterward. Cleanse it by burying it in earth, resting it on selenite, or using sound or smoke, and it can be charged in sunlight or moonlight. Avoid abrasive cleaners that could dull the polish. Store it with similar rocks and wrap it in cloth when traveling. A quick wipe with a soft cloth keeps the polished surface glossy.
identify: Indigo gabbro is dark grey to black with white or silvery feldspar flecks and sometimes subtle blue sheen. Dalmatian jasper has spots of brown and black on a cream background, while black tourmaline is a single crystal rather than a speckled rock. Dyed or painted stones sometimes pass as merlinite, but real gabbro has natural, irregular patterns. Because it is a rock, individual pieces vary widely in pattern and tone.

faq.a: Indigo gabbro is a dark igneous rock, speckled with white or silver feldspar, that formed slowly from magma underground. In the crystal trade it is polished into spheres and palm stones for grounding and shadow work.

faq.q: Is indigo gabbro the same as merlinite?
faq.a: They are often sold under the same trade names, and both describe dark rocks with pale flecks. Merlinite can also refer to a black stone with white dendritic patterns, so check the seller's description.

faq.q: Can indigo gabbro go in water?
faq.a: Yes. It is a hard, stable rock, so rinsing with lukewarm water is safe. Dry it afterward to keep the polish bright, and avoid harsh chemicals or abrasive scrubbing.
